set.tovw: Lead grade C (treasure thread): two accounts; home placed at Ferry and Eighth Streets by the local paper
set.pl: His home at the corner of Ferry and Eighth Streets, Niles (Niles Republican, 26 Jun 1902)
set.t: Urban corner lot: look only. A c.1900 Niles Sanborn would show the house and yard.
pinev: Home named by the Niles Republican, 26 Jun 1902, as the corner of Ferry and Eighth Streets; the pin is still at city level and has not yet been moved to that corner.

tw-mi-niles-andrew-jackson-gold.st: The local paper called him perhaps the wealthiest Black resident of Berrien County; he ran a carrying business, owned several lots and had a habit of hiding his money. He was said to have tried to tell where he had buried gold coin before the stroke took his speech. No find was reported.
src: Niles Republican, 26 Jun 1902, p. 3, 'His Secret Unrevealed' (from the Daily Star; Newspapers.com image 1101384144, PC (a))
